name: pre_eclampsia
title: Management of Pre-eclampsia in a Pregnant Woman
description: Pregnant woman at 34 weeks gestation presents for routine antenatal visit with new-onset headaches, visual disturbances, and lower extremity oedema. Covers recognition and initial management of pre-eclampsia with severe features at a primary health centre, including magnesium sulphate administration and referral.
clinicalInvariants: Gestational age: 34 weeks; Gravida 3 Para 2 with uncomplicated prior pregnancies
Chief complaint: persistent headaches for 4 days, bilateral pedal oedema for 1 week, occasional blurred vision
Clinical findings: BP >= 150/100, urine protein 3+, brisk reflexes (3+), bilateral pitting oedema 2+, no clonus
Foetal assessment: cephalic presentation, FHR 142 bpm, active foetal movements, SFH 33 cm
Assessment: pre-eclampsia with severe features; mild anaemia of pregnancy
Management: magnesium sulphate loading dose (Pritchard regimen), antihypertensive, urgent referral to secondary/tertiary facility
Key SP responses: previous pregnancies uncomplicated, family history of hypertension in mother, headache not relieved by paracetamol, no seizures or epigastric pain
